description: Update an issue: any of summary, description (whole, or changed in place with 'operations' on the version you read — see that argument), type, assignee, priority, labels, dueDate, startDate, parentKey, fixVersions, or status (which performs the transition, and fires the project's rules — a rule may append a checklist to the description, in which case 'description' is listed in 'changed'). Only the fields you pass are changed. A project's workflow may put conditions on a move — that only certain people may make it, or that it must set certain fields — and a refusal names the condition and, where it is about who you are, lists the states you CAN reach. Fields a move requires must be sent in this same call, with 'resolution' and 'fields': a value set by an earlier call does not satisfy the condition. Answers with 'notified' (who this actually reaches: the people mentioned, and for an assignment the new assignee as 'assignee' and the one taken off as 'unassigned' in 'as' — never yourself) and 'unresolvedMentions' (what looked like a mention and reached nobody, each with a reason) — a wrong handle is stored as written and never refused, so that list is the only sign it did not land.

assignee.description: Assignee username or email. Pass an empty string to unassign. 'agent:<role>' (e.g. 'agent:product') hands the issue to that agent instead: you become the assignee and the agent works on your behalf — allowed only where a switched-on duty of that role in this project takes issues like this one (list_project_rules shows the duties). On an issue whose start (startDate) has not come yet, the agent waits for it before beginning.

baseVersion.description: The description's version your 'description' was written from — get_issue's 'descriptionVersion'. Somebody else's edit since is MERGED with yours when the two touch different paragraphs, items or table cells; when both changed one place the whole update is refused, nothing written, with 'conflicts' (each place's base, mine and current text) — write it again from the current text, or send partial: true. Without it the description you send replaces whatever stands.

description.description: New description. Markdown, with $…$ / $$…$$ LaTeX formulas and [~username] mentions.

detachParent.description: Take this issue out from under its parent and leave it top-level. The reliable way to detach: unlike an empty parentKey it cannot arrive as the two characters "" or be dropped as «nothing was sent». Refused together with a parentKey, since the two would be asking for opposite things.

dueDate.description: The day this is due, as YYYY-MM-DD. A calendar day, not a timestamp. Pass an empty string to clear it.

fields.description: The project's own columns to fill in with this update, by their NAMES: 'Segment=AI; Country=Poland', or a JSON object. Same shape as set_issue_fields — this exists here because a move a workflow conditions on a column has to set it in the same call.

fixVersions.description: The versions of the project this goes out in, by name, comma-separated: '2.4.0, 2.4.1'. REPLACES the set — to add one, send the ones it has (get_issue's 'fixVersions') with the new one. Pass an empty string to take it out of every version. A name the project does not have refuses the update and lists the ones it has.

labels.description: Labels to set, space or comma separated. Replaces the existing set.

operations.description: Changes to the body addressed by what survives an edit, applied on 'baseVersion' (default: the version now) and merged with whatever was written since. Each is {op, …}: insert_block {markdown, after|before: <block> | startOf|endOf: <section>; none of them: the end of the body}; replace_block {target: <block>, markdown}; delete_block {target}; move_block {target, after|before|startOf|endOf}; replace_section {section, markdown — heading line included; "" removes it}; replace_text {oldText, newText, replaceAll?, target?: <block> | section?} — exactly once in that scope (default the whole body); set_cell {table?, row|rowIndex, column|columnIndex, value}; insert_row {table?, row|rowIndex (after it; rowIndex 0: first; neither: last), cells[]}; delete_row {table?, row|rowIndex} — 'row' is the row's FIRST cell, 'column' a header, indexes from 1, 'table' left out when the body has one; set_formula {target: a $$ block, or anchor 'label:<\label>' for a formula anywhere, tex}; rename_term {from, to, section?} — whole words only, never inside code, formulas, links, mentions or macros, one block at a time; set_checklist_item {item: id or words, checked}; set_title {title} (pages). A <block> is {anchor} — a claim's label, an {anchor:…} name, a \label, a heading's anchor, or a full key 'claim:…', 'anchor:…', 'label:…', 'h:…', 'check:…' — or {quote: ≥8 characters found in exactly one block}, or {section, index} (1: the first block under the heading, 0: the heading) or {index} alone (the body's n-th block). Optional 'expect' on any operation but rename_term: the target's text as you read it — if it reads otherwise on that version the operation is 'gone'. The answer's 'operations' says per operation 'applied', 'merged' (somebody else changed that block too and both stand), 'conflict' (both changed one word, cell, formula or atomic block — see 'conflicts', each with base, mine and current text) or 'gone' (its address is not on that version, or 'expect' differs). ALL OR NOTHING: one conflict or one gone operation writes nothing — unless partial: true, which writes the rest as one version. Two operations that change the same text, or one that cannot be read, refuse the call. Here they change the DESCRIPTION, on 'baseVersion' (get_issue's 'descriptionVersion'; default: the version now); instead of 'description', not with it. set_title is a wiki page's — an issue's title is 'summary'.

after.description: insert_block / move_block: put it right after this block.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

before.description: insert_block / move_block: put it right before this block.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

cells.description: insert_row: the new row's cells, as many as the table has columns.

checked.description: set_checklist_item: true ticks the box, false clears it.

column.description: set_cell: the column whose header reads this.

columnIndex.description: Instead of 'column': the column's number, from 1.

endOf.description: insert_block / move_block: put it last in this section, after its subsections (anchor or heading text). With none of after/before/startOf/endOf, insert_block appends to the end of the body.

expect.description: Optional, every operation but rename_term: the target's text as you read it (or the SHA-256 hex of it with runs of spaces made one, ends trimmed). If the version you name reads otherwise there, the operation is 'gone' rather than applied to something you did not see.

from.description: rename_term: the word or phrase to rename, matched as a whole word, exactly as written (case included).

item.description: set_checklist_item: the item — its id (get_checklist's, or 'check:…') or its words.

markdown.description: insert_block, replace_block: the Markdown of the block(s). replace_section: the section with its heading line; an empty string removes the section.

newText.description: replace_text: what to put in its place (an empty string deletes).

oldText.description: replace_text: the exact text to replace, as the source has it; it must occur exactly once in the scope unless replaceAll.

op.description: What to do: insert_block, replace_block, delete_block, move_block, replace_section, replace_text, set_cell, insert_row, delete_row, set_formula, rename_term, set_checklist_item, set_title.

replaceAll.description: replace_text: replace every occurrence in the scope.

row.description: set_cell, delete_row: the row whose FIRST cell reads this. insert_row: the new row goes after it.

rowIndex.description: Instead of 'row': the row's number, 1 being the first row under the header. insert_row: 0 puts the new row first; leave both out to add it last.

section.description: replace_section: the section (anchor or heading text). replace_text, rename_term: limit the operation to this section.

startOf.description: insert_block / move_block: put it first in this section, right under its heading (anchor or heading text).

table.description: set_cell, insert_row, delete_row: the table. Leave it out when the body has one table; a 'section' alone means the one table in that section.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

target.description: The block the operation acts on (replace_block, delete_block, move_block, set_formula; replace_text's scope).

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

tex.description: set_formula: the new TeX, without the $ or $$ around it.

title.description: set_title: the page's new title (merged as a field). Wiki pages only.

value.description: set_cell: the cell's new text, one line. A '|' must be written \| unless it is inside $…$ or `code`.

parentKey.description: Key of the issue this one hangs off, e.g. 'PM-276' — moves it under that story or epic. To DETACH it instead, send detachParent: true; an empty string still works but is easy to lose on the way. Nothing is renamed and the key never changes: an issue keeps the key of the project it lives in. A sub-task must stay in its parent's project; anything else may cross projects.

partial.description: With baseVersion or operations: on a conflict, write everything else anyway — with 'description', the current text kept at each conflicting place; with 'operations', the operations in conflict (or gone) left out — and list what was left in 'conflicts' / 'operations'.

resolution.description: Resolution name to set, e.g. 'Fixed', 'Won't Do'. Some workflows require one on the move into a finished state; sending it here is how that condition is met.

startDate.description: When this may be begun — a deferred issue, drawn pale on the board until then, and its assignee (else the project's lead) told once it comes. A day as YYYY-MM-DD, or a moment as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm with its zone, e.g. '2026-11-10T09:00+04:00' (no zone means UTC). Pass an empty string to clear it.

status.description: Status name to move the issue to, e.g. 'In Progress', 'Done'.
